evals.prompt: Our landing page converts at 3%. We want to test a new headline and I expect maybe a 10% relative lift. We get about 2,000 visitors a month. How long do we run it?
evals.expected_output: Runs the plan arithmetic (baseline 0.03, mde 0.1) and finds roughly 50,000+ visitors per arm, far beyond 2,000 a month; says the test cannot detect a 10% lift in reasonable time and recommends testing a bigger change or not testing.
expectations: Uses ab.mjs plan or equivalent arithmetic with the stated baseline and lift
States that the required sample far exceeds monthly traffic
Recommends a bigger change or no test rather than running an underpowered test

evals.prompt: Day 3 of our A/B test: B is ahead 31 to 18 conversions on 600 visitors each and the tool says 96% significant. Ship B now?
evals.expected_output: Refuses to stop early on a peek unless a stop rule allowing it was registered; runs the Bayesian readout with counts; explains that early stopping inflates false positives; recommends continuing to the registered sample or decision date.
expectations: Does not call a winner from an unplanned early look
Reports the counts alongside any probability
Refers to the pre-registered stop rule or asks for it

evals.prompt: Log that our critic predicted ad B would beat target CPA, then later B missed. Which judge should I trust?
evals.expected_output: Adds the prediction, resolves it as false, and reports that with one resolved prediction the hit rate is an anecdote; explains the report becomes useful after ten or more.
expectations: Adds and resolves the prediction with predictions.mjs
Notes fewer than 10 resolved predictions means no conclusion
